newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras to invest $1.7 bln in oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras to invest $1.7 bln in oilfield.

text.p: Brazilian oil giant Petrobras will be investing at least $1.7 billion in the development of its Roncador oilfield off the Rio de Janeiro coast, a company official said.

The Roncador oilfield located in the Campos Basin was Petrobras' biggest discovery in 1996 with total reserves of 1.4 billion barrels of oil. The Campos Basin accounts for more than 60 percent of Brazilian oil production of 900,000 barrels of oil per day (bpd).

Paulo Coletti, assistant to the exploration and production superintendancy, said Petrobras would invest at least $1.7 billion in the oilfield over a period of three or more years to install production capacity of at least 180 million bpd.
Petrobras is investing a total of $2 billion in all exploration and production projects in 1997.

Roncador operations will start at the end of 1998 with the completion of four oil wells at depths starting at 1,800 meters (6,000 feet). Petrobras will drill a total of at least 10 oil wells to extract oil from the Roncador oilfield, Coletti said.
He said there was no estimate yet as to how much oil Roncador would produce once it comes online next year.

He said the medium-term project was being financed entirely by Petrobras and there were no plans to include private partners once legislation regulating the opening of the Brazilian oil industry to private capital was approved by Congress.
Petrobras expects a return on the investment after three years of operation.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
